correctness.rationale: For binary rotation classes (no reversal or complement), every deletion from the same cyclic run produces one descendant, giving the r-run bound. Nonconstant binary necklaces have even run count. Even n: alternating words have only two descendants and other words have at most n-2 runs. Odd n: r=n-1 forces one double run, and deletion symmetries create at least one collision (n=5,7) and two independent collisions for n>=9; other words have <=n-3 runs. The family 0^a(10)^t1^b with a,b>=2 has 2(t+1) distinct run descendants anchored by the long 0 and 1 runs; given constructions attain all cases. This proves the exact piecewise M(n). Independent full-necklace enumeration through n=14 produced all claimed maxima and class counts; infinite claim relies on the run argument.
